title: tiny feedback loop proto notes
content:
Context: quick personal sketch for a small, low-friction feedback loop that surfaces user signals from hosted API calls into short actionable cycles for product and model teams. Goal: surface high-signal failures or surprising outputs to enable fast triage + small UX nudges (instead of big eval runs).

Ideas/why this matters:
- Many product regressions are subtle and only show up in tiny proportions of traffic; current telemetry misses because averaging hides tails.
- Want a lightweight path from endpoint -> customer-visible nudge / triage ticket -> small model/prompt tweak -> measurement within days.
- Keep opt-in per-tenant, low perf cost, privacy-preserving (no raw user content stored beyond short hashes/metadata).

Core components (sketch):
1) On-request sampler: probabilistic but biased to low-confidence / long responses / high-latency requests / high edit-distance from top-k generations. Tag each sample with anonymized hash and minimal context metadata.
2) Micro-report UI: small modal or inbox in console with 1-sentence snippet, reason (low-cof, hallucination-like), quick action buttons (mark false positive, create triage ticket, request immediate rollback on tenant model variant).
3) Triage pipeline: creates lightweight triage cards in internal queue with links to request id, sample metadata, simple repro: prompt + sanitized context + model version. Allow product/ML to assign and annotate.
4) Fast experiment loop: ability to push small prompt patches or routing rule changes at tenant-level (canary to 1% -> 10% -> 100%). Autoscore before/after with same sampler to validate.

User stories (rough):
- As a product manager, I want to see the top 10 flagged tenant samples from the last 24h so I can prioritize fixes.
- As an ML engineer, I want a repro that contains sanitized prompt + model + tokens so I can write a targeted prompt patch and run quick offline eval.
- As an SRE, I want sampling to add <1% p99 latency and be configurable by tenant and by route.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Sampling triggers on at least 3 signal heuristics (confidence, latency, length delta) and stores <= 2k bytes per sample.
- Console panel shows flagged samples with quick actions and ability to create triage cards.
- Triage card includes anonymized sample, model version, route, and link to internal ephemeral replay that can be executed by engineers.
- Canary workflow: apply prompt patch to 1% of tenant traffic and observe metric delta within 48h.

Metrics to track:
- Time from flagged sample -> triage card creation
- Fraction of flagged samples leading to actionable changes
- Mean tokens / request for sampled vs baseline
- False positive rate (manual label fraction)
- Latency and cost delta introduced by sampling

Technical notes / constraints:
- Privacy: no PII persisted. Use client-side hashing + server-side salt per-tenant. Store only token counts, mask full content in UI unless user consents.
- Storage: short TTL (7–30 days) for samples; index by tenant and route for fast scan.
- Sampling bias: implement weight function w = base_rate * f(confidence, latency, length_ratio); default base_rate=0.001 but tunable per-tenant and per-route.
- Runtime: try to fit into the inference path with minimal blocking; prefer emitting async sideband events to ingest pipeline.

Open questions / TODOs:
- UI ownership: product console or a separate "micro-triage" app?
- Data retention policy: default 14 days or 7? legal to confirm.
- Granular consent: should enterprise customers be able to opt-out entirely at account level?
- What counts as a hallucination signal besides low confidence? semantic similarity to knowledge base? hallucination classifier costs?

Quick rollout plan (alpha):
- Week 0: implement server-side sampler + event schema, internal-only sampling for 0.1% of traffic.
- Week 2: internal console card viewer + triage queue prototype.
- Week 4: invite 3 internal product teams to opt-in, iterate on signals and UI.
- Week 8: tenant opt-in in hosted console + basic canary controls.

Notes to self:
- Keep scope tiny for first pass; separate the nicer-to-have sentiment and KB-checkers for later.
- Sync with legal on hashing approach before any customer opt-in.
- Link: see JIRA-PLAT-987 for ingestion proto and feature flag work.

Random brainstorm bullets:
- Could add a lightweight "suggested prompt patch" generator (LLM-based) that proposes 1–2 sentence guardrails for offending prompts.
- Aggregate dashboard that surfaces recurring prompt patterns across tenants (privacy risk, need safe-guarding).
- Reward-flow for customers who label samples (small credits) to reduce false positives.

End of notes. This is intentionally messy — coming back later to split into proto tasks.
